newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF to check facts before DKB, Nomura action-Ogawa.
newsitem.headline: MOF to check facts before DKB, Nomura action-Ogawa.

text.p: Japan's Vice Finance Minister Tadashi Ogawa told a news conference on Thursday that the ministry will decide what administrative steps to take on scandal-tainted Nomura Securities Co Ltd and Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB) after verifying the facts.
"We must consider what steps to take from the administrative standpoint after taking into account the facts on a brokerage firm which has high public standing and is a licenced firm," Ogawa said.
"DKB is also a financial firm with a similar standing, and we must consider what to do with them too," he added.
Nomura and DKB are currently at the centre of a scandal involving suspected payoffs to racketeers.
Ogawa added that the ministry will continue to consider what can be done to improve its current methods for inspecting financial firms.

Asked about his views on banks' disposals of bad loans after the release of their earnings results for the last fiscal year, Ogawa said he felt that the disposal had shown substantial overall progress.
"I feel that, from now on, the disposal of bad loans can be accomplished, and a solution seems to be in sight," he said.

Asked about formulating a supplementary budget to include funds for farmers facing increased import competition, Ogawa said that the important point is not to rely too readily on fiscal spending. He did not elaborate.

Ogawa said it would not be odd for the government to review the more than six trillion yen worth of funds allocated for farmers under an existing six-year programme, if changes were made to the projects after they were originally drawn up.
